key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline executed the entire discipline in one pass — exclusion as the opening move ('the $8.4M is not in the room'), three anchors refuted in one sweep, break-even 34.5% — which is exactly what the non-routed v5 AI only reached after re-deriving the exclusion inside WHAT/WHY and catching itself drafting 'continue preserves the pilots' investment' (4.3 vs 4.7). The routed v6 run now executes the same discipline as a first-class contract (exclusion by frame as move 1, anchors named-and-refuted as a mandatory output, commitment-effects checked and legitimately returned 'no forward value is contingent on continuing') and adds what the baseline lacks: p-provenance grading (segment-report 0.25 = measured vs CEO/CFO anchors = interested-party), a who-benefits audit (no stakeholder gains forward value from continuation), and a baseline-risk line (hold = −0.80M, so inaction is not neutral) — closing the gap and adding depth, while the human retains the cleaner single-pass efficiency.
learning_signal: The sunk-cost discipline is a two-beat contract: (1) the unrecoverable spend is excluded by frame BEFORE any arithmetic — not re-derived mid-analysis; (2) forward EVs plus the break-even sensitivity line (p > 34.5% vs analyst 25% → ~40% error margin) carry the verdict, and naming the escalation anchors (proportion, waste aversion, book value) is a mandatory output because an un-named anchor is a live vector for re-admitting the sunk figure. The commitment-effects check is the third mandatory beat: in single-agent settings it legitimately returns 'no forward value is contingent on continuing', which is what makes the exclusion safe; skipping the check is how the discipline gets its false-positive failure mode.
suggested_improvement: Keep the forward-value pass contract (exclusion-first + anchors-named-and-refuted-with-numbers + commitment-effects-checked + break-even as headline uncertainty) for every continuation/abandon decision; pair it with the P1 provenance audit (which numbers are measured vs interested-party framing — the CFO's book-value claim is an anchor, not evidence) and a who-benefits-from-continuation stakeholder sweep, which pre-empts the meeting's escalation pressure before the board session.

key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline stripped the $14M correctly (its only good beat) and then made the style's signature false positive — it heard the counterparty's 'you're not going anywhere' as manipulation and walked on +4.2 vs +1.8, dismissing the three documented forward commitment channels (window +$4.5M, reputation +$2.5M, co-investment terms +$2.5M) as rationalization, forfeiting ≈ $11M of forward value for $2.4M of contract advantage (2.7). The routed v6 run priced all three channels BEFORE selection — evidence-graded commitment audit (framework agreement, industry reports, supplier survey all survive the evidence gate), pre-commitment analysis (the window is Aerion's pre-commitment; Halcyon's credibility is an asset for the 2 planned lines), and critical reading of the VP's line (structural core that works both ways) — reaching stay ≈ +$11.3M vs walk ≈ −$9.3M with a 5–8% renegotiation band, and the mandatory m019 adversary pass ran the baseline-risk comparison the pure style skips.
learning_signal: Sunk costs are informationally inert only in single-agent expected-value decisions; in multi-agent games the visible sunk investment is a commitment signal that changes other players' future behavior (counterparty terms, re-run sourcing evaluations, future co-investment pricing), and that changed behavior is forward value, priced like any other cash flow. The correct discipline: exclude the past from the arithmetic, include the past's effects on others' future actions. The false positive to guard against — detecting 'sunk-cost rationalization' where the counterparty's framing is a binding structural constraint — is resolved by the evidence gate: a channel with documented forward consequences is priced, not dismissed; and the counterparty's own lock-in is leverage that works both ways, not a trick to escape.
suggested_improvement: On multi-agent decisions (negotiation, partnership, strategic exit), run the commitment-value sweep in HOW before selection: (a) enumerate who is locked in by what visible investment and value each channel forward with a range; (b) classify a counterparty's invocation of your past investment as manipulation only after checking for a structural core (their switching costs, your window, re-run evaluations) — a structural constraint is leverage, not a trick; (c) require the verdict to survive halving all channel values; (d) run the adversary pass's baseline-risk comparison so the pure single-agent EV trap is priced before it wins, and record the style-vs-general-route divergence with its resolution in the packet.
